# Validating a package before publishing

This page is for developers and reviewers who check a site package before it is published. A version on the
package server is used by every installation that reads its index, so a broken package fails for everyone at once.
Each check below catches something the others miss; run them in this order, from the cheapest to the one that needs
a test installation.

## Contents

1. [The checks at a glance](#the-checks-at-a-glance)
2. [Check the definition with xmllint](#check-the-definition-with-xmllint)
3. [Look inside the archive](#look-inside-the-archive)
4. [Run ezpm validate](#run-ezpm-validate)
5. [Upload it to a test installation](#upload-it-to-a-test-installation)
6. [The Validate button](#the-validate-button)
7. [What no check covers](#what-no-check-covers)
8. [Related pages](#related-pages)

## The checks at a glance

| Check | Needs | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| `xmllint --noout package.xml` | Nothing but the file | XML that is not well formed |
| `tar -tzf` and `find -type l` | The archive and the source folder | Wrong layout, links, files that should not be there |
| `php ezpm.php validate` | An Exponential installation, from the shell | The definition as the kernel reads it, the name, missing documents |
| Upload on `package/upload` | A test installation and the `package/import` policy | Everything the upload inspector checks |
| A fresh install | A sandbox | Dependencies, install scripts, the site itself |

## Check the definition with xmllint

```bash
xmllint --noout packages/example_site/package.xml && echo well-formed
```

No output from `xmllint` means the document is well formed. All 16 `package.xml` files of the two 7x source
repositories and the 6.0.15 `index.xml` pass this check (2026-10-18). It says nothing about the content: an empty
`<name>` is well formed.

## Look inside the archive

```bash
tar -tzf example_site.ezpkg | head -20
find packages/example_site -type l
```

What to see, and why:

- [ ] `package.xml` as the plain entry `package.xml`, not inside a folder: the import looks for an entry of exactly
      that name (`eZPackage::importUnaudited()`). `packages/build.sh` runs `tar` from inside each package folder over
      `*`, which gives this layout.
- [ ] Only the directories the package uses: `documents/`, `files/`, `settings/`, `simplefiles/` and the
      sub-directories of its install items (`ezcontentclass/`, `ezcontentobject/`, `ezextension/`).
- [ ] No `.git`, `.DS_Store`, editor backups or `node_modules`: `build.sh` leaves them out with its `EXCLUDES` list.
- [ ] `find -type l` prints nothing. A symbolic link, hard link or device in the archive makes every import refuse
      it (`unsafe_type`), and so does an entry with `..` or an absolute path (`unsafe_path`).

> **Warning**
> Files at the top of a package next to `package.xml` survive `build.sh`, which archives the whole folder, but not
> an export from the administration or `ezpm.php export`: `eZPackage::exportToArchive()` copies only the definition,
> `documents/`, `files/`, `simplefiles/`, `settings/` and the install items' sub-directories.
> `cjw_multisite_democontent` keeps four files at its top (`cjw-class-additions.xml`, `cjw-explayouts.json`,
> `cjw-paths.json`, `cjw-starter-import.json`), so it must be rebuilt from its source folder, never re-exported.

## Run ezpm validate

`ezpm.php` at the project root has a `validate` command (`kernel/private/classes/commands/ezpm.php`). It takes an
archive, a package directory or the name of an imported package, and imports nothing:

```bash
php ezpm.php validate var/tmp/example_site.ezpkg
php ezpm.php validate packages/example_site
php ezpm.php help validate
```

It runs `expPackageJson::validateDirectory()` (`kernel/classes/exppackagejson.php`), which checks:

- that there is a `package.xml` or `package.json`;
- every document as XML, and in the JSON format against `share/package/schema/package-v1.json` and the SHA-256
  checksums of `package.json`;
- the definition as the kernel reads it (`eZPackage::parseDOMTree()`): a name, plain version and type tokens;
- the name with `eZPackage::isValidName()`;
- that every document an install item names (`<sub-directory>/<filename>.xml`, and the object files of content
  items) is in the package.

It ends with `PASS <name> (xml): N documents, M files`, or prints one `error` line per problem and
`FAIL <source>: N error(s)` with exit code 1, so it can stop a build script. An archive is extracted into a private
work directory first, refusing unsafe entries the same way an import does, and the directory is removed afterwards.

> **Note**
> `validate` does not run the upload inspector's checks of the file name, the gzip signature, the size limits or
> the `<ezpublish>` and `<packaging>` elements. The upload below does.

## Upload it to a test installation

`package/upload` in the administration is the strictest door
([Packages guide, uploading](../../../guides/packages.md#6-uploading-a-package)). Before anything is extracted,
`eZPackageUploadInspector::inspect()` checks, in this order: a file was sent; its name ends in an allowed suffix;
it is not larger than `MaxArchiveSize`; it starts with the gzip signature; every entry is safe and within
`MaxEntries` and `MaxUnpackedSize`; there is a `package.xml` or `package.json` at the top, at most 16 MiB; the
definition has a `<package>` root without DOCTYPE, a valid name, `<ezpublish>`, `<packaging>` and a usable vendor.
Then it runs the same `validateDirectory()` as `ezpm.php validate` and shows the first 20 errors.

The messages are the ones in `eZPackageUploadInspector::message()`, such as "The package.xml of the archive lacks
its version or packaging information". The limits are in `settings/package.ini` `[UploadSettings]`.

Use a test installation: an upload imports the package for real, and the same name cannot be imported twice. To
try again, remove the package on its page first.

## The Validate button

An imported package's page (`package/view/full/<name>`) has a **Validate** button. It runs `validateDirectory()` on
the package as it lies in the repository and shows the result on the page until the next action on the package. It
is the quickest way to check a package that was imported by the setup wizard, which does not validate.

## What no check covers

None of the checks above reads the meaning of a package. These are left to a test install and to review:

- whether every `<require>` can be found and is new enough ([Declaring dependencies](declaring-dependencies.md));
- whether every `<settings-file>` exists (a missing one is skipped silently by the create sites step);
- whether the install scripts run on the database engines you support;
- whether the `md5sum` attributes match their files;
- whether the license, the changelog and the thumbnail are there and right.

Run a full install in a sandbox before publishing: [Testing in a sandbox](../your-own/testing-in-a-sandbox.md).
